messages:
SupportOps: @eng-sre urgent: ACME (high-tier customer) reports sudden p95/p99 latency regressions for text-generation on hosted-api since ~2055549000. p95 from ~120ms -> 850ms, p99 up to ~2.3s. Customer doing normal traffic; spike correlates with higher IO wait and GPU driver warnings in our logs. Escalating for infra-level investigation. :alarm:

Alice Chen: looking. Root cause candidates: storage IO tail, driver/kernel change, or batching/timers. Any infra changes rolled out last 24h?

Ravi Patel: I rolled kernel 5.15->6.1 on a subset of dedicated nodes yesterday (~2055549200) and also pushed NVIDIA driver 535.104 -> 537.67 on some GPU pools. No config changes to batching.

Elena Morales: on runtime side we see increased KV cache miss rate and longer iterate times in the serving trace. Request queues show heavy serialization at nvme completion.

infra-bot: deploy 2055549201 (kernel-rollout/6.1) succeeded on nodes gpu-dedicated-{a,b,c,d} :white_check_mark:

Alice Chen: okay please paste dmesg / nvme logs from an affected node. Also capture iostat/top and GPU errors.

Ravi Patel: grabbing logs now. Samples:

```
[2055549302.123] nvme0: I/O timeout, removing queue 4
[2055549302.124] nvme0: failed command: nvme list-ns returned -110
[2055549302.125] NVRM: GPU at 0000:65:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus
[2055549302.126] kernel: blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 1234567
```

Alice Chen: that nvme timeout + GPU off bus is worrying. Could be controller/firmware or new kernel/driver interactions. Please run these quick probes (on an affected node):

```
# check nvme queue & health
sudo nvme list
sudo nvme smart-log /dev/nvme0
# monitor iostat
iostat -x 2 5
# dmesg tail
sudo dmesg | tail -n 100 | egrep -i "nvme|NVRM|GPU has fallen off the bus|blk_update_request"
# check kernel blk-mq stats
cat /sys/block/nvme0n1/queue/*, /proc/interrupts | egrep nvme
```

Elena Morales: running bpftrace snippet to get per-process block latency distribution, I'll paste output.

Ravi Patel: iostat snap:

```
Device            r/s     w/s   rkB/s   wkB/s rrqm/s wrqm/s  r_await w_await aqu-sz  %util
nvme0n1         125.00   80.00 10240.00 4096.00    0.00   0.00   8.42  25.91   3.40  95.12
```

Ravi Patel: nvme smart-log shows rising media_errors and temp spikes. Also firmware v5.3.0 on controller.

Alice Chen: timeline so far: kernel + driver + nvme controller on same window. We need to triage: 1) confirm if kernel/driver or storage. 2) mitigate for customer (ACME). 3) remediation plan.

Elena Morales: mitigation options for customer: route ACME to older model variant (smaller mem footprint, less KV cache pressure) and reduce concurrency / max_tokens. We can toggle routing in ~2 min.

SupportOps: please do that while infra continues to investigate. Customer is open to temporary throttling if it reduces 99s.

Ravi Patel: starting rollback of NVIDIA driver on gpu-dedicated-a,b now to 535.104. Rolling in 2-node batches. Not rolling kernel yet.

deploy-bot: rollback-driver job 2055554332 started on gpu-dedicated-a :gear:

Alice Chen: also please isolate a healthy node from the set and run fio with mixed workload to reproduce tail. Use this fio job:

```
[global]
ioengine=libaio; direct=1; bs=128k; rw=randrw; rwmixread=70; iodepth=32; numjobs=8; runtime=120
```

Ravi Patel: rollback finished on node a. Initial checks: dmesg no new nvme timeouts on node a and p99 for local test reduced. Rolling node b next.

Elena Morales: routing ACME to model v2.12 (previous stable) and lowering max_tokens to 512 and concurrency to 8 for that tenant. Health checks started.

SupportOps: notifying ACME: "we're routing traffic to a safe variant and throttling burst for now; investigating infra change. We will update in 30m."

Alice Chen: running bpftrace script /opt/tools/io-latency.bt. Output: heavy tail at ~15ms -> 400ms for nvme0 operations tied to process redpanda-worker (our prefetcher).

Ravi Patel: after rolling node b, both nodes a/b show lower iowait and the reproduction fio shows no tail. Node c still noisy. Suspect specific hardware/firmware on c interacting with new kernel/driver. Opening ticket with cloud provider for nvme firmware upgrade/rollback.

Alice Chen: plan: immediate mitigations done (route+throttle+driver rollback on two nodes). Next: 1) Continue rollback on remaining affected nodes 2) vendor engagement for firmware/drive replacement 3) if rollback not possible everywhere, schedule customer routing to dedicated unaffected pool 4) postmortem.

Ravi Patel: vendor ticket opened (ticket# CLOUD-9072). They asked for nvme smart logs and dmesg. Sent. Also requested stable firmware image.

Elena Morales: observed reduced KV cache misses after routing, p95/p99 for ACME dropped to ~210ms / 640ms. Still higher than baseline but customer accepts interim.

SupportOps: ACME reply: "Thanks, latency improved but still seeing occasional spikes. Please keep us posted." :+1:

Alice Chen: assigning action items: - Ravi: complete driver rollback on remaining nodes and coordinate vendor firmware (due 2055554500) - Elena: keep ACME on v2.12 + throttles, collect traces for 2h (due 2055555521) - SupportOps: customer comms and status updates (ongoing) - Alice: write incident ticket and lead postmortem once stable (due 2055557000)

Ravi Patel: note for postmortem: hypothesized root cause = interaction between kernel 6.1 blk-mq changes and certain NVMe controller firmware causing queue stalls; NVIDIA driver may have exacerbated GPU recovery events but storage appears primary. Need controlled test matrix (kernel x nvme fw x nvidia driver).

Alice Chen: good. Keep thread updated. If vendor confirms firmware bug, we might ask for rolling hardware replacement for nodes with firmware v5.3.0 and consider pinning kernel/driver combinations until validated.

deploy-bot: healthcheck for ACME route change passed at 2055554375 :white_check_mark:

SupportOps: ACME confirms p99 down to ~380ms after rollback + routing. We'll leave this incident open for monitoring for 2 hours. Closing only after stable and vendor plan.

Elena Morales: logging a follow-up eval to simulate long-running KV cache churn under new kernel in staging.

Alice Chen: thanks all. Will capture this thread in the incident ticket for the postmortem.

SupportOps: closing note for now: mitigation working, vendor engaged, customer updated. Will reconvene if p99 returns >1s. :lock:
